name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
pattern: One-leg hip hinge: the trunk tips forward and the free leg swings back as one line while the standing hip bends.
setup: Stand on one foot, knee soft, weight over the middle of the foot.
Hold the weight in the hand opposite the standing leg, arm long.
Hips level and facing the floor, like headlights pointing down.

steps.text: Push your hips back and tip forward; the free leg rises behind you in line with your back.
Stop when your trunk is near level or your back starts to round.
Drive the standing heel into the floor and bring the hips through to stand tall.

cues.cue: Keep both hip bones level, pointing at the floor.
cues.why: Resisting the hip opening is what loads the gluteus medius; it is among the top exercises for it.

cues.cue: Head to back heel in one straight line.
cues.why: The leg moving with the trunk keeps the movement at the standing hip and the spine still.

cues.cue: Soft knee, fixed angle; do not squat down.
cues.why: The work stays on the hip extensors and hamstrings.

cues.cue: Weight in the hand opposite the standing leg.
cues.why: Contralateral loading raised glute and back activity in a loaded single-leg RDL.

cues.cue: Grip the floor with the whole foot.
cues.why: Balance limits the load; a stable foot lets the hip do the work.

breathing: Breathe in as you hinge down, out as you stand up.

tempo.note: Slow down; balance is easier with control.

mistakes.name: Hips open up
mistakes.looks: The free-leg hip rotates up toward the ceiling and the toes turn out.
mistakes.fix: Point the back toes at the floor; keep hips level.
mistakes.why: It turns the hinge into a twist and takes load off the glutes.

mistakes.name: Back rounds
mistakes.looks: You reach the weight to the floor by curling the spine.
mistakes.fix: Stop higher; reach with the hips, not the hands.
mistakes.why: Range should come from the hip, not the lower back.

mistakes.name: Standing knee bends deep
mistakes.looks: The standing knee bends a lot and the hips drop instead of going back.
mistakes.fix: Lock in a soft knee and push the hips back.
mistakes.why: It turns the hinge into a squat and moves the work to the quads.

safety: Use a wall, rack or kickstand stance until balance is steady.
Hamstring strain history: keep the range short and build slowly.

variants.change: Back toes stay on the floor for balance; most weight on the front leg.
Support or a guided bar: easier balance, more load possible.
At the top, drive the free knee up to hip height.
Pass the weight hand to hand at the top or under the leg.
Weight on the same side as the standing leg: less balance and glute medius challenge.
Hold the bottom position for time.

harder: single-leg RDL on an unstable surface

subtypes.name: Kickstand RDL
subtypes.change: Back foot stays down on its toes, a half step behind.

subtypes.name: Single-leg RDL with knee drive
subtypes.change: Ends each rep with the free knee driven up to hip height.

motion.basis: Right leg stands; left (L keys) is the free leg. No study in the set reports full joint angles; values are estimates from the hinge geometry (back leg in line with trunk, so hipFlexL about 0 to -5). Muscle findings from diamant2021, mo2023 and collings2023.
